Messages.Author: Ben Peal
Messages.Body:
.

Hello, V:TES players!

On Saturday, November 1, Boston will be hosting the Create-A-Clan
tournament - where you get to design your own vampires!

Create-A-Clan
Saturday, November 1
noon 'til we're done
3 rounds plus finals
Your Move Games in Somerville
www.yourmovegames.com
Free!

The rules are quite restrictive (and a bit lengthy), but they have
to be. :)

It's recommended that for your crypt, you put cards in sleeves and
put print outs of your vamps in front of the cards. For tools and
help for creating your vampire cards, check out Damnan's site at:

http://www.almadrava.net/damnans/

Tools found here:

http://www.almadrava.net/damnans/downloads.htm

We'll have the following prize categories:

- Winning Player
- Best Artwork
- Best Clan That Didn't Use Dominate
- Most Creative/People's Choice

If you have any other recommendations for prize categories, email me!

THE RULES

* Clan must have a name and sect (can't choose Anarch)
* You may have a unique Hunting Ground for your clan, which must
also have a name. (Hunting Grounds with the same name will
contest!)
* All vamps in clan must be of that sect
* All vamps must have a unique name (Vamps with the same name
will contest!)
* Keep the names clean, kids!
* Clan must have three "in-clan" disciplines, and the set of three
must not be the same as that of an official clan
* Vampires may not have Bloodlines disciplines, though Bloodlines
discipline library cards may be used (in the outferior, or perhaps
via Vial of Elder Vitae or the like)
* Multi-discipline cards may not be used
* No more than two vampires of the same capacity
* No two vampires may share the exact same discipline spread
(For example, AUS POT QUI and AUS POT qui are ok, but not
two vamps with AUS POT QUI)
* No two vampires of 5-cap or less may share the same superior
discipline
* "Out-of-clan" disciplines may not be shared by more than two
vampires
* No two vampires of the same capacity may share the same "out-of-clan"
discipline
* A vampire may only have an "out-of-clan" discipline if it has all
three "in-clan" disciplines
* A vampire must spend more points on "in-clan" disciplines than on
"out-of-clan" disciplines
* Vampires get points for disciplines, titles, and specials as
follows, where X is the capacity of the vampire:
- 2-4 cap = X-1
- 5-8 cap = X
- 9-10 cap = X+1
* Disciplines as follows:
- Basic discipline: 1 point
- Superior discipline: 2 points
* Titles as follows:
- Primogen/Bishop min 6-cap, 0.5 points
- Prince/Archbishop min 8-cap, 1 point
- Justicar/Cardinal min 10-cap, 1.5 points
- Priscus min 8-cap, 1 point
- "This vampire has 2 votes" min 8-cap, Independent only, 1 point
* A clan may have only one Justicar or Cardinal
* A Prince or Archbishop must be of a specific domain. Allowable
domains are those of V:EKN Princes, except those of "official"
vampires (i.e. no Prince of Boston). The list of domains can be
found here: www.white-wolf.com/vtes/veknPrinces.html
* Special abilities as follows:
- +1 bleed: min 6-cap, 1.5 points (max +1 bleed)
- +1 strength: min 6-cap, 1.5 points (max +1 strength)
- +1 intercept: min 9-cap, 1 point (max +1 intercept)
- +1 stealth: min 9-cap, 2 points (max +1 stealth)
- +1 strength when in combat with a specific sect: no min, 1 point
(may be chosen in addition to +1 strength, above)
- + 1 bleed when bleeding a specific sect: no min, 1 point
(may be chosen in addition to +1 bleed, above)
* A vampire may have only one special ability (in addition to a title
and disciplines), and only one vampire per clan may have each special
ability
* If you have 0.5 points left over, too bad
* Your crypt must contain only vampires from your clan
* You may have no more than 2 copies of each vampire in your crypt

It's recommended that you email your crypt to me ahead of time so
I can make sure it's legal. My email address is fu...@mindstorm.com.
Feel free to email me with other questions you may have about the
tournament, as well. (Note: I'll be in Barcelona for the EC until
Wednesday, October 22, so I may be slow in responding)

See you there!

- Ben Peal, Prince of Boston
fu...@mindstorm.com

Messages.Author: Ben Swainbank
Messages.Body:
vincen...@hotmail.com (Vincent Price) wrote in message news:<a60ff9bd.03110...@posting.google.com>...

> So what happened for the tournament?!

Well, there may be an "official" report pending. But I can provide
some details.

The event was a blast. We had 10 players and really high production
values on the cards. Most of them can be seen off the Boston V:TES
site here:

http://www.darkwindrising.com/vampire/cac1/cac1.asp

I was quite proud of my Mazzeri clan -- even though I had just plucked
images for a Google search and pasted it together with Paint and
Publisher. But everyone else outclassed me -- busted out the
previously unseen photoshop skills and did some fun stuff.

Lots of joke clans, as you can see, so the whole day was filled with
exchanges like "Bleed with Battle Dwarf Torgulon". "Sluffleupagus to
block"... Goofy fun.

Sadly DJ's Aztecs aren't up yet. He won the art prize with a very nice
set of vamps.

Playwise, it was interesting how non-broken the decks were. They
didn't really seem stronger or weaker than normal stuff. My
CEL,FOR,VIC rush deck totally flamed out getting 0 vp for the day.
Lots of combat defense out there and despite my Krazy Kraken's Kiss
Kombo the deck lacked both killing power and defense.

I didn't stick around for the finals, but I understand that John
Mason's Hair Bands won the day. So, it turns out that by using OBF and
DOM together you can make a strong bleed deck. Who woulda thunk it?!?

It's a cool format and I think we all want to try it again. Maybe
spice it up with those crazy Bloodlines disciplines next time...

-Ben Swainbank
